comparisons.peer_summary: Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2024 increased 15%, reflecting higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels and growing demand.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVDA explicitly cite the normalization of customer channel inventory levels as a key driver for their respective fiscal year 2024 financial results. AMD reported that its Embedded segment net revenue decreased by 33% primarily because 'customers continued to normalize their inventory levels,' indicating that the prior year's demand was inflated by stockpiling. In contrast, NVDA reported that its Gaming revenue increased by 15% specifically reflecting 'higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels,' suggesting that the normalization of inventory constraints had shifted from a headwind in 2023 to a tailwind being resolved in 2024, allowing for renewed growth. The comparison highlights how the same macroeconomic phenomenon (inventory normalization) impacted peer companies' segment revenues differently due to varying product cycles and demand strengths.

sentences.text: Embedded net revenue of $3.6 billion in 2024 decreased by 33%, compared to net revenue of $5.3 billion in 2023.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.
Gaming revenue for fiscal year 2024 was up 15%.
The increase reflects higher sell-in to partners following the normalization of channel inventory levels and growing demand.

comparisons.peer_topic: QCT segment revenue drivers and EBT margin change
comparisons.peer_summary: QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 increased primarily due to higher handset revenues driven by $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments from major OEMs and higher automotive revenues from new vehicle launches with Snapdragon products, partially offset by lower IoT revenues; QCT EBT as a percentage of revenues increased primarily due to these higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Similar to AMD, QCOM identified the normalization of customer inventory levels as a primary driver for its fiscal 2024 handset revenue recovery. While AMD's Embedded segment still faced a 33% revenue decline despite normalization, QCOM reported a 9% overall revenue increase driven by '$2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments... primarily driven by the normalization of customer inventory levels, which were elevated in the prior year.' This comparison shows that for QCOM, the normalization of elevated inventories from the prior year directly unlocked significant volume growth in 2024, whereas AMD saw continued demand weakness in its Embedded segment even as inventory normalized.
